title: Acceptance criteria: streamed protocol resilience, schema negotiation, and tool-handOff semantics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Scope: Define acceptance criteria for the next-generation structured-output protocol and tool/function-calling behaviors when responses are streamed. The goal is to make streamed structured responses resilient to partial/parsing failures, allow schema negotiation between client and model runtime, and specify deterministic tool handoff semantics (retry, idempotency, ordering) for production workloads. This ticket captures product-level requirements, test cases, rollout constraints, and measurable success metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Schema negotiation handshake: The API accepts an optional header/param 'schema_version' (string) and returns an agreed 'effective_schema_version' in the initial stream metadata. If the server cannot offer the requested version, it must emit an explicit 'schema_negotiation' event with 'offered_versions' and a chosen 'effective_schema_version'.

Streaming boundary contract: Stream must include well-documented boundary events: 'stream.meta' (initial), 'stream.obj_chunk' (object fragment), 'stream.obj_end' (object complete), and 'stream.eos' (end-of-stream). Clients must be able to reconstruct JSON objects deterministically from 'obj_chunk' fragments even when interleaved with plain text tokens.

Partial-object resilience: If a parser error occurs mid-stream (malformed JSON chunk), the runtime will emit 'stream.parse_error' containing 'cursor' and 'error_class' ('transient'|'permanent'). For 'transient' errors the server will attempt up to 2 automatic repair passes (e.g., bracket rebalancing/truncation heuristics); if repair succeeds the server emits 'stream.obj_repaired' and resumes. If repair fails or error is 'permanent', the stream must include a structured 'fallback_object' (conforming to a lenient schema) and return a 207-like code in final metadata.

Tool call semantics during streaming: When the model issues a tool call while streaming, the runtime must emit a 'tool.call' event with: tool_id, input_digest, request_id, and schema_hint. The tool call must be persisted until the runtime receives a tool.response with matching request_id. If the tool fails transiently, runtime retries according to the tool policy (0s, 1s, 2s backoff) up to 3 attempts and emits 'tool.retry' events. Permanent tool failures must produce a 'tool.failure' event and a structured fallback described in 'fallback_strategy' (see fallback criteria).

Idempotency and dedup: Each tool invocation must include 'request_id' and 'client_request_id'. Replayed or duplicate requests from the client or runtime should be identified and ignored by downstream integrations; acceptance tests must verify a single side-effect for duplicate invocations with identical request_id.

Ordering guarantees: Tool calls initiated by a single streaming response must preserve relative ordering. If tool B depends on tool A's output, it is the runtime's responsibility to serialize events so that 'tool.call.B' is not confirmed until a successful 'tool.response.A' or an accepted fallback has been emitted.

Graceful fallback modes: System supports two fallback flavors declared in initial metadata: 'strict' (fail-fast: stream ends with error metadata and no fallback_object) and 'lenient' (server emits best-effort fallback_object when structured output cannot be produced). Acceptance: default is 'lenient' for host API; enterprise customers can opt into 'strict' via configuration.

Latency & finality signals: For streaming structured responses that include tool calls, the runtime must provide a 'stream.finality' event containing final_status ('ok'|'partial_with_fallback'|'error') and a concise 'diagnostic_code' string. Finality must appear within 3s of the model deciding the final token under normal load for objects < 2KB.

Compatibility and versioning: Old clients (no schema_version) must receive an 'effective_schema_version' header and may be served a legacy-compatible object. New schema fields must be additive; acceptance tests verify that clients with older schemas do not break when extra fields are present.

Operational observability: Each streamed structured response must emit tracing information (trace_id) and per-tool call latency metrics. The platform must surface counts of parse_errors, repaired_objects, tool_retries, and finality outcomes in the console dashboard within 10 minutes of occurrence.
Security: Tool call payloads must be scrubbed of sensitive tokens before they appear in any user-facing logs. Acceptance includes a verified KMS-enforced redact test described in Test Plan.
success_metrics: <0.5% of streamed structured responses result in 'finality'='error' in production after rollout
<0.2% of streams require automatic parse repair steps after canary
Tool invocation dedup success: 100% idempotency for duplicate request_id in integration tests
Observability coverage: parse_error and tool_retry events available in console and logs within 10 minutes for 95% of events
test_plan: Unit tests for stream parser (correct chunk reassembly, malformed chunk heuristics), integration tests using a mock tool that returns chunked JSON and intermittent transient failures, E2E SDK tests for JavaScript and Python clients verifying schema negotiation header roundtrip, and chaos tests that inject random byte corruption into streamed chunks. Key testcases: 1) interleaved text + obj_chunks -> deterministic reconstruction; 2) mid-stream malformed chunk repaired -> emits obj_repaired; 3) permanent parse error -> lenient fallback_object emitted; 4) tool transient failure with retries -> single applied side-effect; 5) idempotent replay -> no duplicate side-effects. See test harness in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tests/structured_streaming_v2
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: 1) internal staging (team-only) for 72h; 2) limited canary (5% of traffic with structured_output_v2=true) for 7 days; 3) expanded canary (25%) for 5 days if metrics pass; 4) 50% rollout for 3 days; 5) global GA. Rollback criteria: parse_error rate > 1.0% or tool side-effect duplication observed. Requires coordinated release with SDK minor version bumps (JS/Python) and runtime-1.20 deployment windows.
staging_checks: All unit/integration tests passing in CI
No regressions in API response shapes for legacy clients
Security review sign-off and KMS redaction verification
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict versus lenient fallback — chose lenient as default to minimize customer-visible failures; strict available as enterprise opt-in.
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STR/Structured+Output+V2 (internal) contains schema negotiation wire format and example sequences.
Architecture PR (runtime): github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1897 implements streaming metadata events and repair heuristics.
SDK updates: PRs will add helper reassembly utilities and explicit event handlers for parse_error and obj_repaired.
Privacy: Before logging, payloads are redacted per KMS rules; ENG-4287 owns verification tests.
